units.title: Foundation — Wo JS jo library banane mein lagti hai

lessons.name: Tree — UI asal mein ek ped hai
lessons.desc: Har HTML page ek nested structure hai, aur nested object bilkul wahi shape bana sakta hai.
lessons.what:
Ek tree matlab: ek cheez ke andar aur cheezein, unke andar aur cheezein. Bas.

Tumhara HTML dekho — <div> ke andar <h1> aur <ul>, <ul> ke andar teen <li>. Ye ek ped hai. Sabse upar wali cheez root, andar wali children, aur jiske andar aur kuch nahi wo leaf.

Analogy: ek almari mein 3 draawer, har draawer mein 2 dabbe, har dabbe mein saaman. Almari = root, draawer = children, saaman = leaf.

Ab yahi shape hum JS object se bana sakte hain. Aur yahi poori library ki neev hai — kyunki hum HTML likhne ki jagah object banayenge, aur baad mein us object ko dekh kar asli HTML banayenge.
lessons.why:
Agar UI ek object hai, to UI ko compare karna, copy karna, badalna — sab data ka kaam ban jaata hai, DOM ka nahi. Aur data ke saath khelna DOM ke saath khelne se 100 guna sasta hai. React ki poori speed isi ek soch se aati hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek node ke paas do cheezein honi chahiye: wo kya hai (type), aur uske andar kya hai (children). Baaki jo bhi extra info ho — class, id, onClick — wo props mein daal do.

Har node ka shape same rakho. Same shape matlab ek hi function sabko handle kar lega. Ye design decision hai, majboori nahi — aur ye tumhare kaam ko aadha kar dega.

lessons.name: Recursion — khud ko bulane wala function
lessons.desc: Tree ke saath kaam karne ka natural tarika. Base case bhool gaye to stack phat jayega.
lessons.what:
Recursion matlab ek function jo apne hi andar apne aap ko bulata hai.

Iska use tab hota hai jab problem "chhoti versions of the same problem" mein tootti ho. Tree exactly aisa hai: poora ped process karo = root process karo + har child ke liye wahi kaam dobara.

Analogy: almari khaali karni hai. Tum kehte ho "har draawer khaali karo". Draawer khaali karne ka matlab "har dabba khaali karo". Dabba khaali karne ka matlab "saaman nikaal do". Wahi ek instruction, har level pe.

Do hisse hote hain: base case (kab rukna hai) aur recursive case (kaise chhota karna hai). Base case bhoole to function kabhi rukega nahi aur browser Maximum call stack size exceeded de dega.
lessons.why:
Hamara render() function recursion hi hoga — Stage A mein poora. Aur baad mein Stage C ki sabse badi seekh yahi hogi ki recursion ko rok nahi sakte. Isliye recursion ko andar se samajhna zaroori hai, sirf "chal gaya" nahi.

Kaise karna hai:

Sochne ka tarika ye hai: maan lo function pehle se kaam karta hai. Sirf ye likho ki "ek node ke liye kya karna hai" aur "children ke liye khud ko bula do". Poore ped ke baare mein mat socho — sirf ek node ke baare mein socho.

Aur haan — browser har recursive call ko call stack naam ke dher mein rakhta hai. Jitna gehra ped, utna ooncha dher.

visual.cap: Call stack: har andar wali call upar chadhti hai. Jab tak sabse gehri call return nahi karti, koi bhi call khatam nahi hoti — isliye recursion ko beech mein pause karna namumkin hai.

for loop ke andar await/return galat jagah lagane se sirf pehla child process hota hai. Result adhoora aata hai par error nahi milti — isliye output hamesha count karke check karo.
Bahut gehra tree (10,000 level) plain recursion se crash karega. Ye Stage C ki asli wajah hai.

lessons.name: Closure — function ka apna secret dabba
lessons.desc: Function apne bahar ki variables yaad rakhta hai. useState isi ek cheez pe khada hai.
lessons.what:
Jab tum ek function ke andar dusra function banate ho, to andar wala function bahar wale ki variables ko yaad rakhta hai — chahe bahar wala function kab ka khatam ho chuka ho. Isko closure kehte hain.

Analogy: tum ek kamre mein gaye, ek parchi pe number likha, kamra band kar diya. Ab tumhare paas ek chhoti khidki hai jisse tum us parchi ko padh aur badal sakte ho. Baaki kisi ko wo parchi dikhti hi nahi. Wo khidki = closure.

Definition: A closure is a function bundled together with references to the variables from the scope in which it was created.
lessons.why:
useState ka poora jaadu yahi hai. Component function baar-baar chalta hai, par state kahin bahar "yaad" rehti hai, aur setState ek chhota function hai jiske paas us yaad tak pahunchne ki khidki hai. Closure samajh gaye to hooks 10 minute mein samajh aayenge.

Kaise karna hai:

Sabse aam pattern: ek "factory" function jo kuch variables banata hai aur unko chhune wale chhote functions return karta hai. Bahar wale ko sirf wo chhote functions milte hain — variable seedha nahi.

Ye encapsulation hai — data ko chhupana aur sirf soch-samajh ke rakhe hue raaste dena. Library design ka sabse purana aur sabse kaam ka tareeka.
gotchas: Loop ke andar var use karoge to sab closures ek hi variable pakdenge. let use karo — har iteration ka apna variable banta hai.
Closure purani value ko "freeze" nahi karta, wo variable ko point karta hai. Variable badla to closure ko nayi value dikhegi. Ye stale-state bugs ki jad hai.

lessons.name: DOM ke wo 7 function jo hum baar-baar use karenge
lessons.desc: Poori library sirf inhi calls se DOM banati hai. Aur koi jaadu nahi.
lessons.what:
Browser tumhe kuch simple functions deta hai jinse tum page ke elements bana aur badal sakte ho. React inhi ko use karta hai — bas bahut soch-samajh ke aur bahut kam baar.

Hamari poori library sirf inhi 7 se chalegi:

  • document.createElement("div") — naya element banao
  • document.createTextNode("hi") — sirf text ka node
  • parent.appendChild(child) — andar daalo
  • parent.removeChild(child) — nikaal do
  • parent.replaceChild(naya, purana) — badal do
  • el.addEventListener / removeEventListener — click wagera
  • el.setAttribute / removeAttribute — class, id wagera
lessons.why:
Ye janna ki "DOM ke paas sirf itne hi auzaar hain" tumhe confidence deta hai. Jab tum React ka source padhoge, tumhe wahi 7 calls dikhengi. Koi chhupa hua API nahi hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek important baat: attribute aur property alag cheezein hain. setAttribute("value", "hi") HTML mein likhta hai; el.value = "hi" asli live value badalta hai. Inputs ke liye property chahiye, warna user ka typed text reset ho jaayega.

Isi tarah class HTML mein hai par JS mein property ka naam className hai — kyunki class JS ka reserved word hai. React ne yahi naam apnaya, isliye hum bhi wahi rakhenge.
gotchas: input ke liye setAttribute("value", x) mat karo. el.value = x karo, warna user jo type kar raha hai wo mit jaayega.
removeEventListener tabhi kaam karta hai jab bilkul wahi function reference do jo add karte waqt diya tha. Naya arrow function banaoge to remove chup-chaap fail ho jaayega.
innerHTML se DOM banana tez lagta hai par har baar sab kuch dobara banta hai — focus, scroll, event listeners sab udd jaate hain. Isi problem ko solve karne ke liye ye poora project hai.

lessons.name: Reference vs copy — aur immutability
lessons.desc: Object ko badal dena aur naya object banana — dono mein zameen-aasman ka farak hai.
lessons.what:
JS mein object ek reference hota hai — matlab variable object ko nahi, uske "pate" ko pakadta hai. Do variable ek hi object ko point kar sakte hain.

Mutation = wahi object badal dena (obj.x = 5). Immutability = purana chhod do, naya object banao ({...obj, x: 5}).

Analogy: mutation matlab kitaab ke ussi page pe overwrite karna. Immutability matlab naya page likhna aur purana page waise ka waisa rakhna. Purana page bacha rahega tabhi tum compare kar paoge ki kya badla.
lessons.why:
Hamara reconciler purane tree aur naye tree ko compare karega. Agar humne purana tree mutate kar diya, to compare karne ke liye purana bacha hi nahi — dono same dikhenge aur kuch update nahi hoga. Ye Stage B ka sabse tricky bug hai aur ye chup-chaap hota hai, error nahi deta.

Kaise karna hai:

Do sasti checks yaad rakho:

Object.is / === do references ko compare karta hai, andar ka content nahi. Yahi wajah hai ki naya object banane se React ko turant pata chal jaata hai ki "kuch badla".

Shallow compare matlab sirf ek level andar dekhna. useEffect ka deps array shallow compare hi karta hai — isliye har render pe naya object dep mein daaloge to effect har baar chalega.
gotchas: Array ke methods do tarah ke hote hain: push/splice/sort purana array badalte hain, map/filter/concat naya dete hain. UI ke liye hamesha naya wala use karo.
Nested object ko {...obj} se copy karoge to sirf upar ka level copy hoga — andar wale objects abhi bhi share ho rahe hain.

units.title: Mental Model — UI ek function hai

lessons.name: Imperative vs Declarative
lessons.desc: Purana tarika: har step batao. Naya tarika: manzil batao.
lessons.what:
Imperative matlab tum browser ko har kadam batate ho: "is div ko dhundo, uska text badlo, is button ka class hatao, ye li add karo."

Declarative matlab tum sirf ye batate ho ki abhi screen aisi dikhni chahiye. Kaise pahunchna hai, wo library ka sar-dard.

Analogy: imperative = taxi driver ko har turn batana ("yahan left, ab right, ab seedha"). Declarative = bas address bata dena. Address batana isliye behtar hai kyunki jab traffic badle to tumhe kuch nahi karna padta.
lessons.why:
Imperative code mein bug isliye aate hain kyunki tumhe har possible transition handle karni padti hai. 3 states hain to 6 transitions. 5 states hain to 20. Declarative mein sirf 5 "screen kaisi dikhe" likhne hote hain — transitions library nikalti hai. Bug ki jagah hi khatam ho jaati hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Declarative banane ke liye library ko current screen aur chahiye wali screen dono pata honi chahiye, taaki wo farak nikaal sake. Isi ko reconciliation kehte hain — aur yahi is poore project ka dil hai.

Matlab: declarative UI ki keemat ye hai ki library ko purani UI yaad rakhni padti hai. Ye trade-off yaad rakhna — memory kharch karke code ki complexity kam ki ja rahi hai.

lessons.name: UI = f(state)
lessons.desc: Ek formula jo poori library ka contract hai.
lessons.what:
Ek line: screen pe jo dikh raha hai wo sirf data ka function hai.

Matlab agar mujhe tumhara state object de do, main bata sakta hu ki screen exactly kaisi dikhegi. Screen mein koi chhupi hui yaad nahi honi chahiye.

Definition: UI = f(state) means the rendered output is a pure function of application state — same state in, same UI out, no hidden memory in the DOM.
lessons.why:
Ye contract hi sab kuch mumkin banata hai. Isi ki wajah se time-travel debugging, server rendering, hot reload, testing — sab possible hain. Aur isi ki wajah se tum bina dare state badal sakte ho, kyunki library screen ko wapas sahi bana degi.

Kaise karna hai:

Iska seedha matlab ye hai ki hamari library ka public API sirf do cheezein hai: ek tarika UI describe karne ka (createElement), aur ek tarika state badalne ka (setState). Baaki sab andar ka kaam hai.

Aur ek chhupa hua niyam: f ko pure hona chahiye — matlab same state pe same output, aur beech mein koi side effect nahi (fetch, timer, DOM chhedna). Side effects ke liye alag jagah chahiye — isi zarurat se useEffect paida hota hai.
gotchas: Component ke andar fetch, setTimeout ya document.title = ... mat likho. Wo function ko impure banata hai aur render do baar chalne pe do baar chalega.
DOM ko state ki tarah mat treat karo. "input mein kya likha hai" state mein hona chahiye, DOM se padha nahi jana chahiye.

lessons.name: Hamari library ke 4 layers
lessons.desc: Poore project ka naksha — abhi dekh lo, phir har phase apni jagah baith jaayega.
lessons.what:
React ko log ek cheez samajhte hain, par wo asal mein 4 alag-alag layers hain, ek ke upar ek. Hum bhi wahi 4 banayenge, ussi order mein.

1. Element layer — createElement. UI ko plain object mein describe karta hai. Isko DOM ka pata bhi nahi hai.
2. Renderer layer — render. Object tree ko asli DOM mein badalta hai. Browser-specific.
3. Reconciler layer — purana vs naya compare karke minimum change nikalta hai. Ye sabse dimagi hissa hai.
4. Scheduler layer — kaam ko chhote tukdon mein todta hai taaki browser atke nahi.
lessons.why:
Ye alag-alag rakhna sirf safai nahi hai — yahi wajah hai ki React Native exist karta hai. Layer 1, 3 aur 4 same rehte hain; sirf layer 2 badal jaata hai (DOM ki jagah native views). Ye architecture ka sabse bada sabak hai: jo cheez badal sakti hai usse alag rakho.

Kaise karna hai:

Hum jaan-boojh kar teen stage mein banayenge, taaki har agli layer ki zarurat tumhe khud mehsoos ho:

Stage A = layer 1 + 2 (createElement + render). Kaam karega, par har update pe sab kuch dobara banega.
Stage B = layer 3 add (reconciler + hooks). Ab sirf zaroori DOM badlega, state bhi milegi.
Stage C = layer 4 add (Fiber + scheduler). Ab bade tree pe bhi page atkega nahi.

Har stage ke end mein ek phase hai jiska naam "deewar" hai — wahan hum jaan-boojh kar tod ke dikhayenge ki current stage kahan fail hota hai. Wahi tumhara "requirement kyu padi" wala jawab hoga.

lessons.name: Element object — sirf teen cheezein
lessons.desc: type, props, children. Bas. Aur children props ke andar rehte hain.
lessons.what:
Virtual DOM element ek plain object hai jo kehta hai "yahan ye cheez honi chahiye". Wo asli DOM node nahi hai — wo sirf ek parchi hai.

Definition: A virtual DOM element is a lightweight plain-object description of a piece of UI. It is a description, not a thing.

Analogy: architect ka naksha vs asli ghar. Naksha banane mein 10 rupaye lagte hain, ghar banane mein 10 lakh. Isliye 20 naksha bana ke phenk do — koi dikkat nahi. Ghar 20 baar mat banao. React yahi karta hai: naksha sasta, ghar mehnga.

Shape ye rahega: { type, props } jahan props.children ek array hai. Children ko props ke andar rakhna ek soch-samajh ka decision hai — isse component ko children ek aam prop ki tarah milte hain.
lessons.why:
Ye object hi wo cheez hai jise hum Stage B mein compare karenge aur Stage C mein tukdon mein process karenge. Iska shape simple aur uniform rakhna baad mein hazaron line ki complexity bachaata hai.

Kaise karna hai:

createElement(type, props, ...children). Rest parameter (...children) se tum jitne chaaho children de sakte ho. props null ho sakta hai — to khaali object bana lo.

Aur ek chhota par bada decision: agar koi child string ya number hai, to usko bhi ek element bana do jiska type "TEXT_ELEMENT" ho. Isse har child ka shape ek jaisa ho jaata hai.

lessons.name: TEXT_ELEMENT — text ko bhi element banana
lessons.desc: Ek chhota decision jo aage 4 jagah "if" lagane se bachaata hai.
lessons.what:
Sabse aasan raasta ye hota: children mein string ko as-is chhod do, aur render ke waqt check karo "agar string hai to text node bana do".

Hum ye nahi karenge. Hum string ko bhi ek element object bana denge jiska type "TEXT_ELEMENT" hai. Ab render, reconcile, commit — sabko ek hi shape milta hai.
lessons.why:
Isko uniform representation kehte hain, aur ye library design ka sabse bada practical sabak hai: ek extra object bana ke tum 10 jagah ki special-case branch bacha lete ho. Har special case ek jagah hai jahan bug chhup sakta hai. React ka asli code text ko thoda alag handle karta hai (performance ke liye), par hum simplicity chunenge — aur ye trade-off decisions.md mein likhna.

Kaise karna hai:

nodeValue naam jaan-boojh kar chuna hai — DOM ke text node ki property ka naam bhi wahi hai. Isse render mein hum bina kisi mapping ke seedha props copy kar sakte hain.

Aur children: [] zaroor rakho, chahe text ke children kabhi na hon. Kyunki node.props.children.map(...) har jagah bina check ke chal jaayega.
gotchas: false, null, undefined ko TEXT_ELEMENT mat banao — React unko render nahi karta. {cond && <div/>} ka false screen pe "false" nahi likhna chahiye. Inko filter kar do.
0 ko filter mat kar dena! {count && <div/>} mein count 0 ho to React "0" print karta hai. Falsy check karte waqt 0 aur "" ko bachana.

lessons.name: Ye function DOM ko chhuta kyu nahi
lessons.desc: Purity aur separation — layer 1 ko browser ka pata bhi nahi hona chahiye.
lessons.what:
createElement ek pure function hai: same input do to same output milega, aur wo duniya mein kuch nahi badalta. Na DOM, na koi global variable.

Definition: A pure function returns the same output for the same input and produces no side effects.
lessons.why:
Iske teen bade fayde hain, aur teeno asli duniya mein use hote hain:

1. Test karna trivial hai — koi browser nahi chahiye, sirf object compare karo.
2. Server pe chal sakta hai — server rendering isi wajah se mumkin hai. Server pe DOM hota hi nahi.
3. React Native mumkin hai — same createElement, alag renderer.

Ek chhoti si purity rakhne ka inaam ye hai ki tumhari library kahin bhi chal sakti hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Isko lagoo karne ka tarika: src/mini-react.js ke element wale hisse mein ek baar bhi document mat likho. Agar likhna pad raha hai, to wo code galat layer mein hai.

Ye ek achhi self-check hai. Har phase ke end mein grep karo: grep -n "document\." src/mini-react.js. Layer 1 mein zero result aana chahiye.
gotchas: Kuch log createElement ke andar hi key nikal kar props se hata dete hain. Abhi mat karo — Phase 7 mein keys aayengi, tab decide karenge.
Element object ko baad mein mutate mat karna (el.props.x = 5). Purane tree ke element bhi wahi object ho sakte hain, aur mutate karne se compare toot jaayega.

lessons.name: render() — recursion se DOM banana
lessons.desc: Ek node ke liye kya karna hai wahi socho, children ke liye khud ko bulao.
lessons.what:
render(element, container) ka kaam teen kadam ka hai: DOM node banao, props lagao, phir har child ke liye khud ko bulao aur result andar daal do.

Ye Phase 0 wale toDom se sirf ek cheez mein alag hai: ab type "TEXT_ELEMENT" bhi ho sakta hai, aur uske liye createTextNode chahiye.
lessons.why:
Ye function poore Stage A ka engine hai. Aur — ye baat abhi note kar lo — ye recursion Stage C mein tootegi. Aaj isko achhe se samjho, taaki jab hum ise linked-list traversal se badlenge tab tumhe pata ho ki hum badal kya rahe hain.

Kaise karna hai:

Order matter karta hai: pehle DOM node banao, phir props lagao, phir children. Children ko pehle karoge to parent hai hi nahi jisme daalo.

Ek design sawaal: container mein appendChild karein ya replace karein? Abhi append karo — Stage A mein hum har baar container khaali karke naya daalenge, aur wahi Phase 5 ki deewar banegi.
gotchas: appendChild sabse aakhir mein karo. Pehle karoge to browser ko har child ke liye alag layout karna pad sakta hai (jab tak tree bahar hai tab tak layout hota hi nahi — ye ek muft optimization hai).
render() ko do baar chalaoge to do copies dikhengi, kyunki appendChild hai replace nahi. Ye Stage A ka jaana-pehchana behaviour hai.

lessons.name: Props lagana — asli complexity yahan hai
lessons.desc: Attribute, property, event, style, children — paanch alag tarah ke props.
lessons.what:
"props lagao" sunne mein ek line lagti hai, par props paanch tarah ke hote hain aur har ek alag treatment maangta hai:

1. children — ye prop nahi hai, isko skip karo.
2. Events (onClick) — addEventListener("click", fn).
3. style object — {color:"red"} ko dom.style.color = "red" banana hai.
4. Live properties (value, checked) — dom.value = x, setAttribute se nahi.
5. Baaki sab (className, id) — property assignment.
lessons.why:
React ke source mein iske liye ek poori file hai (DOMPropertyOperations), aur uski wajah yahi hai ki HTML/DOM ka mapping saaf nahi hai. Ye samajhna ki "React ki complexity ka bada hissa browser ki wirasat sambhalna hai" ek asli architecture insight hai — library ki jatiltaa aksar duniya ki jatiltaa ka aaina hoti hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek hi function updateDom(dom, prevProps, nextProps) likho jo abhi bhi kaam kare aur Phase 6 mein bhi. Stage A mein prevProps khaali object dena. Stage B mein wahi function purane props ke saath dubara use hoga — ek line badle bina.

Ye forward-compatible design hai: aaj ka simple case kal ke complex case ka ek special case ban jaaye. Aisi jagah dhundna aur pakadna hi achhi library design hai.

lessons.name: Pehla chalta hua app — aur uski seemayein
lessons.desc: Kaam karta hai. Par har update pe poora ghar dobara banta hai.
lessons.what:
Ab tumhare paas Stage A poora hai. Ek app likho, chalao, khush ho lo — aur phir usko todo.

Stage A mein update ka matlab hai: container khaali karo, poora naya tree render karo. Isko full re-render ya blow away and rebuild kehte hain.
lessons.why:
Ye "bewakoof" version banana zaroori hai, skip karne wali cheez nahi. Kyunki agla har design decision (reconciler, keys, fiber) sirf tabhi samajh aayega jab tumne khud dekha ho ki isme kya kami hai. Interview mein bhi yahi farak dikhta hai — "React fast hai" bolne wale aur "Stage A mein main ne focus loss measure kiya tha" bolne wale mein.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek chhota rerender() banao jo root.innerHTML = "" karke dobara render kare. State ke liye abhi ek simple module-level variable rakho — asli useState Phase 8 mein aayega.

Aur zaroor: numbers naapo. performance.now() se 100, 1000, 5000 node ke liye render time note karo. Ye numbers Phase 5, 10 aur 14 mein baar-baar kaam aayenge.
gotchas: innerHTML = "" event listeners ko bhi hata deta hai — ye achhi baat hai (memory leak nahi hoti), par iska matlab hai har render pe sabhi listeners dobara lagte hain.
Focus loss ko "CSS se theek kar lenge" mat socho. Ye architectural problem hai, cosmetic nahi. Isko theek karne ka ek hi tarika hai: DOM node ko zinda rakhna.

units.title: JSX & Tooling — Bina build ke, aur build ke saath

lessons.name: JSX asal mein hai kya
lessons.desc: Sirf syntax sugar. Compiler usko createElement calls bana deta hai. Bas itna hi.
lessons.what:
JSX JavaScript ka hissa nahi hai. Browser JSX samajhta hi nahi. Ek compiler (Babel, esbuild, swc) usko padhta hai aur normal function calls mein badal deta hai — tumhare code chalne se pehle.

Definition: JSX is a syntax extension that a compiler transforms into plain function calls before the code ever runs.

Analogy: JSX ek translator ki tarah hai jo tumhari Hindi ko English mein badal ke sahab ko sunata hai. Sahab (browser) ne Hindi kabhi nahi suni. Wo sirf English janta hai.
lessons.why:
Ye samajhna is poore project ki sabse badi "ohhh" wali cheez hai. Jab tum JSX ko compiled form mein dekhoge, to React ka har "jaadu" gayab ho jaayega. <App /> ka matlab hai createElement(App) — aur App bas ek function hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Compiler ko batana padta hai ki kis function mein badalna hai. Purana tarika: file ke upar /** @jsx h */ pragma. Naya tarika: build config mein jsxFactory: "h".

Do rules yaad rakho: chhote akshar wala tag string ban jaata hai (<div> → "div") aur bade akshar wala variable ban jaata hai (<App> → App). Isliye component ka naam capital se shuru hona zaroori hai — ye rule library ka nahi, compiler ka hai.

lessons.name: Bina tooling ke — h(), tagged templates, htm
lessons.desc: JSX ka syntax nahi milega par saara feature milega. Aur zero build time.
lessons.what:
JSX ke bina teen raaste hain:

1. Seedha h() likho. Zero setup. Thoda bracket-bhari dikhta hai par bilkul saaf hai ki ho kya raha hai.
2. Chhote helper banao — const div = (p, ...c) => h("div", p, ...c). Ab div({}, h1({}, "hi")) likh sakte ho.
3. Tagged template literals — htm library (3KB) tumhe html`<div></div>` likhne deti hai, browser mein, bina build ke.
lessons.why:
Ye janna zaroori hai ki tooling optional hai. Bahut se log sochte hain React ke liye webpack/Vite "chahiye hi". Nahi chahiye. Tooling ek convenience hai jiski apni keemat hai — aur wo keemat kab jayaz hai ye tum tabhi decide kar paoge jab tumne dono taraf khud khada hoke dekha ho.

Kaise karna hai:

Zero-tooling ka sabse bada fayda: jo file tum likhte ho wahi file browser chalata hai. DevTools mein debug karna trivial hai, koi source map nahi, koi "ye line kahan se aayi" nahi. Seekhne ke liye ye behtareen hai.

Sabse bada nuksaan: har import ek alag network request hai, aur 50 files ka app dev mein dheema lagega. Aur JSX ka aaram nahi milega.
gotchas: htm runtime pe parse karta hai, matlab har render pe thodi cost hai (wo cache karta hai, par cost zero nahi). JSX compile-time pe ho jaata hai — zero runtime cost.
Helper tags (div, h1) global namespace mein bahut naam le lete hain. Ek object mein rakho aur destructure karo.
Bina bundler ke import mein .js extension mandatory hai. Bundler wale code ko copy karoge to import toot jaayega.

lessons.name: Tooling ke saath — kya milta hai, kya jaata hai
lessons.desc: Vite/esbuild add karo aur imaandari se dono taraf ka hisaab likho.
lessons.what: Ek bundler (Vite, esbuild, webpack) teen kaam karta hai: transform (JSX → JS), bundle (50 file → 1 file), aur dev server (HMR, fast reload).
lessons.why:
Kya milta hai: JSX ka aaram; ek network request; minify + tree-shaking se chhota bundle; HMR jisse state bachte hue code reload hota hai; node_modules se import (bina URL likhe); TypeScript, CSS modules, images — sab.

Kya jaata hai: ab tumhara code aur browser ka code alag hain — debugging ke liye source maps chahiye; ek aur config file jo tootegi; node_modules mein 200MB; build time; aur sabse badi baat — ek aur cheez jo tumhe samajhni padegi.

Kaise karna hai:

Ye faisla mechanical nahi, situational hai. Chhota learning project, ek-do file, sikhne ke liye → zero tooling behtar hai, kyunki tum wahi dekh rahe ho jo chal raha hai. Bada app, team, TypeScript, 50+ files → tooling ki keemat wasool ho jaati hai.

Interview mein ye sawaal aata hai. Sahi jawab "Vite use karo" nahi hai — sahi jawab hai "ye kis cheez ke badle kya de raha hai, aur mere case mein kya zyada keemti hai".

units.title: Stage A ki deewar — Har baar sab kuch dobara

lessons.name: Identity — DOM node zinda rehna kyu zaroori hai
lessons.desc: Focus, scroll, selection, animation, video playback — sab node ke andar rehte hain, tumhare state mein nahi.
lessons.what:
Ek DOM node sirf "kya dikhta hai" nahi hai. Uske andar bahut si chhupi hui state hoti hai jo tumhare JS mein kahin nahi hai:

  • Focus kis element pe hai
  • Text selection kahan se kahan tak hai
  • Scroll position kitna hai
  • CSS transition/animation kis frame pe hai
  • <video> kis second pe chal raha hai
  • Uncontrolled input mein user ne kya type kiya

Node delete karte hi ye sab gayab. Naya node banane se ye wapas nahi aata.
lessons.why:
Isko identity kehte hain: "ye wahi node hai ya naya node hai". Aur ye poore reconciliation ka asli maksad hai. Log sochte hain reconciler speed ke liye hai — nahi. Speed ek bonus hai. Asli wajah correctness hai: DOM node zinda rehna chahiye warna app tootta hai.

Ye ek bahut achha interview point hai, kyunki zyadatar log "virtual DOM fast hota hai" wala ratta bolte hain.

Kaise karna hai:

Iska ilaaj ek hi hai: purana tree yaad rakho, naye se compare karo, aur jo node same hai usko chhuo mat — sirf uske badle hue props update kar do.

Isliye Stage B ka pehla kadam code nahi hai, data hai: hume ek jagah chahiye jahan purana tree aur uske DOM nodes ka rishta store ho.
gotchas: Focus ko "render ke baad wapas focus kar denge" se theek karne ki koshish mat karo. Wo cursor position, selection aur IME (Hindi/Chinese typing) sab tod dega.
Ye problem sirf inputs ki nahi hai. Third-party libraries (chart, map, editor) jo DOM node pakad ke rakhti hain, wo poori ki poori toot jaati hain.

lessons.name: Performance — kitna kaam bekaar ja raha hai
lessons.desc: Ek akshar badalne pe 5000 node dobara banana. Naapo, guess mat karo.
lessons.what:
Stage A mein har update ka kaam tree ke size ke barabar hai, chahe change kitna hi chhota ho. Ek counter 0 se 1 hua — poora tree dobara.

Aur DOM banana JS object banane se bahut mehnga hai, kyunki har createElement pe browser ko internal structures banane padte hain, aur appendChild ke baad layout aur paint dobara karna padta hai.
lessons.why:
Numbers ke bina ye sirf feeling hai. Numbers ke saath ye engineering hai. Aur ye habit — "pehle naapo, phir optimize karo" — is poore project se badi seekh hai.

Kaise karna hai:

performance.now() se ms naapo, aur Chrome DevTools ke Performance tab mein recording lo. Do cheezein dhundo: Scripting (JS), aur Rendering + Painting (browser ka kaam).

Ek zaroori observation: agar tumhara update 16ms se zyada leta hai, to 60fps nahi mil sakta — browser ke paas ek frame ke liye sirf 16.7ms hote hain. Ye number yaad rakh lo, Phase 10 mein ye poori kahani ban jaayega.

lessons.name: Solution ka aakaar — diffing
lessons.desc: Purana yaad rakho, naye se milao, farak nikalo. Aur ye O(n) mein karna hai.
lessons.what:
Ab problem statement saaf hai: purana tree aur naya tree diya hai, batao ki DOM mein kya-kya badalna hai.

Ye ek jaani-pehchani computer science problem hai — tree diffing. Aur bura news ye hai ki general tree diff ka best algorithm O(n³) hai. 1000 nodes = 1 arab operations. Bekaar.
lessons.why:
React ne isko O(n) banaya, par muft mein nahi — do assumptions maan kar. Aur yahi is poore project ka sabse bada architecture sabak hai: jab exact solution mehnga ho, to problem ko chhota kar do — soch samajh ke, likh kar.

Kaise karna hai:

React ke do assumptions:

1. Alag type = alag tree. Agar purana <div> tha aur naya <p> hai, to compare mat karo — poora subtree phenk ke naya banao. Ye 99% cases mein sach hota hai.
2. Key se identity milti hai. List mein bachon ko position se nahi, key se pehchaano. (Phase 7)

Ye heuristic hai — matlab hamesha optimal nahi, par practically hamesha kaafi. Ye batana ki "ye heuristic hai, algorithm nahi" tumhe baaki sabse alag kar dega.
gotchas: Ye assumptions "React ki kami" nahi hain — ye soch-samajh ke liye gaye trade-offs hain. Agar tum <div> ko <span> mein badalte ho to poora subtree dobara banta hai, aur ye tumhe pata hona chahiye.
Diffing ka maksad speed se pehle correctness (identity) hai. Ye baat baar-baar bhoolti hai.

units.title: Reconciler — Purana yaad rakho, farak nikalo

lessons.name: Purane tree ko DOM ke saath yaad rakhna
lessons.desc: Element object pe dom field. Simple, aur yahi aage fiber banega.
lessons.what:
Compare karne ke liye humein do cheezein chahiye: purana element tree, aur har purane element ka asli DOM node.

Sabse seedha tarika: jab hum DOM banate hain, to usko element object pe hi laga dete hain — element.dom = domNode. Ab purane tree se DOM tak pahunchna free hai.
lessons.why:
Ye "purana tree + uske DOM nodes" wali cheez ka ek naam hai — instance tree (React ise pehle instances kehta tha, ab fiber tree). Aur is phase mein tum jo bana rahe ho, wo asal mein fiber ka chhota, recursive version hai. Stage C mein hum isi tree ko fiber node bana denge — data wahi rahega, sirf traversal badlega.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek module-level variable rakho: let currentTree = null. Pehli baar mount(), uske baad har baar update():

update(newTree) = reconcile(container, currentTree, newTree, 0) phir currentTree = newTree.

Ek chhota par zaroori sawaal: naya element apna DOM kahan se paayega? Jawab — jab UPDATE case chalega, hum newEl.dom = oldEl.dom kar denge. DOM node purane se naye element ko pass ho jaata hai. Yahi identity bachne ka mechanism hai.

lessons.name: reconcile() — chaar cases
lessons.desc: ADD, REMOVE, REPLACE, UPDATE. Poora function isi table se nikalta hai.
lessons.what:
Function ka signature: reconcile(parentDom, oldEl, newEl, index). index isliye chahiye kyunki humein pata hona chahiye ki parent ke andar ye kaunsa bachcha hai (parentDom.childNodes[index]).

Chaar cases, ussi order mein check karo:

1. !oldEl → ADD: naya DOM banao, parentDom.appendChild
2. !newEl → REMOVE: parentDom.removeChild(parentDom.childNodes[index])
3. oldEl.type !== newEl.type → REPLACE: naya banao, replaceChild
4. same type → UPDATE: DOM pass karo, props update karo, children recurse
lessons.why:
Ye chaar cases exhaustive hain — koi paanchwa case hai hi nahi. Aur yahi achhi library design ki nishani hai: state space ko itna chhota kar do ki tum sabhi cases likh sako aur sabit kar sako ki koi chhoot nahi gaya.

Kaise karna hai:

UPDATE case mein teen kaam hain, ussi order mein:

1. newEl.dom = oldEl.dom — DOM node aage pass karo.
2. updateDom(dom, oldEl.props, newEl.props) — Phase 3 wala function, bina ek line badle.
3. Children ke liye loop: Math.max(oldChildren.length, newChildren.length) tak jao, aur har index pe reconcile(dom, oldChildren[i], newChildren[i], i).

Math.max isliye kyunki children ki ginti badal sakti hai — dono taraf ke undefined apne aap ADD ya REMOVE case bana denge. Ye ek chhoti si khoobsurti hai.

lessons.name: Recursion ki keemat — aur ek warning
lessons.desc: Ye kaam karta hai, tez hai, par ek baar shuru hone ke baad ruk nahi sakta.
lessons.what:
Tumhara reconciler ab tez hai aur sahi hai. Par uski ek property hai jo abhi dikhegi nahi: wo interruptible nahi hai.

Jaise hi update() call hua, wo poore tree pe recursion karega. Beech mein rukega nahi. JS single-threaded hai, matlab jab tak ye function chal raha hai, browser kuch nahi kar sakta — na click sun sakta hai, na paint kar sakta hai, na scroll.
lessons.why:
Chhote apps mein ye bilkul theek hai — 100 nodes 1ms mein ho jaate hain. Par 10,000 nodes pe ye 200ms ka ek "long task" ban jaata hai aur user ko app freeze lagega. Yahi Phase 10 ki deewar hai, aur Fiber ka poora janm isi ek problem se hua.

Kaise karna hai:

Abhi kuch mat karo. Bas notes/ mein likh do: "reconcile recursion hai, isliye ek baar shuru hone ke baad ruk nahi sakta. Rukne ke liye call stack ko chhodna padega."

Ye habit banao — jab bhi tumhe kisi design ki seema dikhe, use turant likh lo, chahe abhi solve na kar rahe ho. Ye "known limitations" list production systems mein sabse keemti document hoti hai.
gotchas: MutationObserver async hai — uska callback microtask mein aata hai, isliye console.log turant nahi dikhega. Ye normal hai.
Agar added/removed abhi bhi zyada aa rahe hain, to kahin type badal raha hoga (jaise conditional rendering se null aur element alternate ho rahe hon).

lessons.name: Position se matching kab tootti hai
lessons.desc: List ke beech mein ek item daalo — har cheez ek jagah khisak jaati hai.
lessons.what:
Socho list hai [B, C] aur nayi list hai [A, B, C]. Position se compare karoge to:

index 0: purana B vs naya A → text badal do
index 1: purana C vs naya B → text badal do
index 2: kuch nahi vs naya C → naya banao

Nateeja: teeno rows chhui gayi, jabki asal mein sirf ek row add hui thi. Aur agar rows mein input the, to unka focus aur typed text galat row pe chala gaya.
lessons.why:
Ye sirf performance ka masla nahi hai — ye correctness ka masla hai. Ek todo list mein checkbox galat item pe tick ho jaayegi. Ek chat mein input ka text galat message pe chipak jayega. Isliye React ki wo "Each child should have a unique key" warning ek gambhir warning hai, nuisance nahi.

Kaise karna hai:

Iska ilaaj ye hai ki matching ka aadhaar badal do. Position ki jagah ek stable identifier — key. Ab reconciler kehta hai: "purani list mein key=B wala kaun tha? Usko naye key=B se milao, chahe wo ab position 1 pe ho."

lessons.name: Keyed reconciliation — map bana ke milao
lessons.desc: Purane bachon ka key→element map, phir naye order mein DOM ko lagao.
lessons.what:
Algorithm seedha hai, teen kadam:

1. Purane children ka ek map banao: key → oldChild.
2. Naye children pe loop chalao. Har ek ke liye map se purana dhundo. Mila to UPDATE (aur DOM node reuse), nahi mila to ADD.
3. Jo purane bache reh gaye (map mein abhi bhi hain), unko REMOVE kar do.

Aur ek chauthi cheez: order theek karna. Reuse kiye hue node purani position pe hain — unko sahi jagah insertBefore se khiskana padta hai.
lessons.why:
Ye O(n) hai — ek map bana ke ek loop. Bina keys ke sahi matching nikalna O(n²) hota (har naye ko har purane se compare karo). Ek Map data structure ne algorithm ki complexity ek class neeche kar di — ye classic CS ka practical use hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Order theek karne ka sasta tarika: naye children pe aage se peeche jaao aur har node ko parent.insertBefore(node, nextSibling) se sahi jagah rakho. Agar node pehle se sahi jagah hai to insertBefore ko skip kar do (warna bekaar DOM operation hoga).

React ka asli algorithm isse thoda smarter hai (wo "last placed index" track karke minimum moves nikalta hai), par idea bilkul yahi hai. Hum simple version likhenge aur decisions.md mein likhenge ki React kya extra karta hai.
gotchas: insertBefore ko har node pe bina soche mat chalao. Wo node ko hata ke dobara daalta hai, matlab focus aur animation udd sakte hain. Pehle check karo ki node pehle se sahi jagah hai ya nahi.
oldByKey.delete(key) karna bhool jaoge to step 3 mein tum abhi-abhi reuse kiya hua node hi delete kar doge.
Duplicate keys se map mein ek hi bachega aur baaki chup-chaap gayab. Dev mode mein duplicate key ki warning zaroor daalo.

lessons.name: key ek prop nahi hai
lessons.desc: Wo reconciler ke liye hai, component ke liye nahi. Ye chhota sa design decision bada hai.
lessons.what:
React mein key component ko milti hi nahi. props.key undefined hota hai. Wo createElement ke waqt props se nikaal kar element pe alag rakh di jaati hai.

Wahi baat ref ki bhi hai. Ye dono "meta props" hain — library ke liye, component ke liye nahi.
lessons.why:
Kyun? Kyunki key ek identity hint hai, ek data nahi. Agar wo prop hoti, to uska badalna ek "props change" ganaa jaata aur re-render trigger karta — jabki key ka kaam hai ye batana ki ye wahi cheez hai ya nayi cheez. Ye do bilkul alag levels ki baat hai.

Ye ek achha general sabak hai: library ke apne metadata ko user ke data se alag rakho, warna dono ghul-mil jayenge aur baad mein alag karna namumkin ho jaayega.

Kaise karna hai:

Hum abhi props.key hi use kar rahe hain (simple), par ab isko theek karna chahiye: createElement mein key ko props se nikaal kar element.key bana do.

Ye ek chhota refactor hai par isko karo — kyunki ye tumhare apne decision ko badalne ka pehla mauka hai, aur decisions.md mein "D6 ko revise kiya, kyunki..." likhna asli engineering journal hai.
gotchas: Refactor ke baad purane code mein props.key reh jaana. Grep karke saare use theek karo, warna keys chup-chaap kaam karna band kar dengi.
key ko number aur string dono allowed hai, par map mein 1 aur "1" alag keys hain. Consistent raho — ya to hamesha String(key) karo.

lessons.name: Function components — type ab function bhi ho sakta hai
lessons.desc: element.type ek function hai to usko call karo, aur uska result render karo.
lessons.what:
Ab tak element.type hamesha ek string tha ("div"). Ab wo ek function bhi ho sakta hai.

createElement(Counter, {start: 5}) ka matlab hai: "yahan Counter naam ka component lagao, usko props {start: 5} do".

Reconciler ko ek nayi baat samajhni padegi: agar type function hai, to uska koi DOM node nahi hota. Usko call karo, jo element wapas aaya usko render karo. Component ek "wrapper" hai jiska koi apna DOM footprint nahi.
lessons.why:
Ye ek badi baat hai: ab tumhare element tree mein do tarah ke nodes hain — host nodes (jinka DOM banta hai) aur composite nodes (jo sirf aur elements banate hain). Har renderer mein yahi do-tarah wala baat hoti hai, aur ye baat Stage C mein aur bhi zaroori ho jaayegi.

Kaise karna hai:

reconcile mein sabse upar ek check: if (typeof newEl.type === "function").

Us case mein: hooks ka context set karo, newEl.type(newEl.props) call karo, jo mila usko reconcile ko de do — ussi parent aur ussi index ke saath. Kyunki component ka apna DOM nahi hai, to wo parent ke andar apni jagah nahi leta; uska bachcha leta hai.
gotchas: Component ko new se mat bulao. Ye plain function call hai — new Counter() galat hai (wo class components ka purana tarika tha).
oldEl.rendered store karna bhool gaye to har update pe component ka purana output khoya rahega aur poora subtree dobara banega.
Component ka naam capital se shuru karo — JSX use karoge to compiler ka rule hai, aur bina JSX ke bhi convention follow karo.

lessons.name: useState — array + index ka jaadu
lessons.desc: Har component ke hooks ek array mein, ek pointer aage badhta rehta hai. Bas.
lessons.what:
Sawaal ye hai: component function har render pe dobara chalta hai, to state kahan bachegi?

Jawab: component ke bahar. Har component instance ke saath ek array joda hota hai — hooks = []. Aur ek pointer hookIndex jo har useState call pe ek aage badhta hai.

Pehla useState → slot 0. Dusra → slot 1. Teesra → slot 2. Agle render mein pointer wapas 0 se shuru hota hai, aur ussi order mein wahi slots milte hain.
lessons.why:
Aur ab tumhe "rules of hooks" ka jawab mil gaya. Hooks if ke andar ya loop ke andar isliye nahi likh sakte kyunki poora system call order pe khada hai. Agar ek render mein 3 hooks chale aur agle mein 2, to slot 1 ki state slot 0 ko mil jaayegi — aur sab kuch chup-chaap ulta-pulta ho jayega.

Ye rule React ki manmani nahi hai; ye is design ka seedha nateeja hai. Aur ye design isliye chuna gaya kyunki iska alternative (har state ko naam dena) API ko bhaari bana deta.

Kaise karna hai:

setState ek closure hai jo apna index aur apna fiber yaad rakhta hai. Wo teen kaam karta hai: slot mein nayi value likho, aur ek re-render schedule karo.

Aur ek zaroori baat: setState(value) ke saath-saath setState(prev => prev + 1) bhi chalna chahiye — kyunki jab do updates ek saath aayein, to purani value pe based update hi sahi jawab deta hai.

lessons.name: setState se re-render — aur batching
lessons.desc: Turant render mat karo. Microtask mein ek baar karo.
lessons.what:
Sabse seedha scheduleUpdate ye hota: turant update(App()) chala do. Ye chalega, par ek problem hai.

Agar ek click handler mein tum teen setState call karo, to teen poore re-render ho jayenge. Do bekaar the.
lessons.why:
Batching matlab: ek hi "turn" ke saare setState ikattha karo, aur ek hi re-render karo. React ye by default karta hai (React 18 se har jagah). Iska faayda seedha hai — kaam teen guna kam. Aur ye ek bahut common architecture pattern hai: kaam ko turant mat karo, ek queue mein daalo aur baad mein ek saath karo.

Kaise karna hai:

Sabse simple batching: ek flag rakho aur queueMicrotask use karo.

queueMicrotask ka matlab hai "abhi wala saara sync code khatam hone ke turant baad chalao, par browser ke paint se pehle". Ye setTimeout(fn, 0) se behtar hai kyunki wo agle frame tak wait karwa deta.

Stage C mein hum isko aur behtar karenge — tab scheduler priority bhi dekhega.
gotchas: setState ke turant baad state variable ko padhoge to purani value milegi. Wo render ke liye "freeze" hai. Ye bug nahi, design hai — aur isi ka jawab functional update hai.
queueMicrotask ke andar error aaye to wo chup-chaap ud sakti hai. try/catch laga ke console.error karo.

Batching ke saath ek nayi cheez zaroori ho jaati hai: agar re-render ke dauraan hi setState hua to infinite loop ban sakta hai. Ek depth counter lagao aur 50 ke baad error do (React bhi yahi karta hai).

lessons.name: Effect render ke baad kyu chalta hai
lessons.desc: Render ke dauraan DOM adhoora hai. Effect ko poora DOM chahiye.
lessons.what:
Definition: A side effect is any work that reaches outside the component — network requests, timers, subscriptions, direct DOM measurement, logging.

useEffect(fn, deps) kehta hai: "fn ko abhi mat chalao. Jab poora render commit ho jaaye aur DOM taiyar ho, tab chalao."
lessons.why:
Do wajah:

1. DOM taiyar hona chahiye. Agar tumhe element ki height naapni hai ya focus lagana hai, to render ke dauraan wo DOM mein hai hi nahi.
2. Render pure rehna chahiye. Render ke dauraan fetch karoge to wo har render pe chalega, aur Stage C mein — jahan render do baar chal sakta hai ya beech mein cancel ho sakta hai — wo bilkul tabaahi hogi.

Ye dusri wajah bahut gehri hai. React ka poora "render pure rakho" wala insistence isliye hai taaki wo render ko rok, phenk aur dobara chala sake. Aur wo Phase 11 ka poora foundation hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Implementation seedha hai: useEffect khud effect ko chalata nahi — wo usko ek queue mein daal deta hai. Reconcile poora hone ke baad, hum queue chalate hain.

Ye "abhi mat karo, list mein daal do, baad mein karo" pattern is project mein teesri baar aa raha hai (batching, effects, aur Stage C ka commit phase). Ye pattern pehchano — ye har bade system mein milega.
gotchas: Effects ko reconcile ke andar mat chalao. DOM us waqt adhoora hai aur agar effect ne setState kiya to tum recursion mein phas jaoge.

flushEffects ke andar effect setState kar sakta hai, jo ek naya render schedule karega. Ye theek hai — par queue ko pehle khaali kar do (q = effectQueue; effectQueue = []) warna list badalti rahegi jab tum us par loop chala rahe ho.

lessons.name: Deps array — kab dobara chalana hai
lessons.desc: Shallow compare. Aur yahi wo jagah hai jahan infinite loops paida hote hain.
lessons.what:
Deps array ka matlab: "in cheezon mein se koi badla ho tabhi effect dobara chalao."

Teen roop hote hain, aur teeno alag hain:

useEffect(fn) — har render ke baad
useEffect(fn, []) — sirf ek baar (mount pe)
useEffect(fn, [a, b]) — jab a ya b badle
lessons.why:
Comparison shallow hai — Object.is se, ek-ek karke. Iska seedha nateeja: agar dep ek object ya array ya function hai jo har render pe naya banta hai, to wo hamesha "badla hua" lagega aur effect har baar chalega.

Aur agar us effect ne setState kiya, to naya render, phir naya object, phir effect, phir setState... infinite loop. Ye React ka sabse common bug hai aur ab tumhe pata hai ki wo hota kyun hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Deep compare kyu nahi karte? Kyunki wo har render pe poore object tree ko ghoomna padega — mehnga aur unpredictable. Shallow compare O(deps.length) hai, hamesha sasta.

Ye ek classic trade-off hai: sasta aur predictable, badle mein user ko thoda soch ke likhna padega. React ne ye chuna, aur useMemo/useCallback is chunav ka seedha nateeja hain — wo hain hi isliye taaki tum reference stable rakh sako.

lessons.name: Cleanup — jo shuru kiya wo band karo
lessons.desc: Effect ek function return kare to wo agli baar se pehle aur unmount pe chalta hai.
lessons.what:
Agar effect ne kuch "shuru" kiya — timer, event listener, subscription, WebSocket — to usko band bhi karna padega. Warna memory leak ya ghost updates (unmounted component pe setState).

useEffect ka contract: agar tum ek function return karo, to library usko do jagah chalayegi — agle effect se theek pehle, aur component ke unmount pe.
lessons.why:
"Agle effect se pehle" wala hissa sabse zyada log miss karte hain. Socho: userId badla, effect dobara chalega. Purane user ka subscription pehle band hona chahiye, warna do subscriptions chalte rahenge. Har baar ek aur judta jayega.

Ye resource lifecycle ka classic problem hai — jo cheez tum acquire karte ho use release bhi karna padta hai. Har system mein yahi hai: file handles, DB connections, locks. React ne ise ek simple contract mein daal diya: "jo return karoge wo band karne ka tarika hai."

Kaise karna hai:

Order zaroori hai: pehle purana cleanup, phir naya effect. Ulta karoge to do cheezein ek saath chalengi.

Unmount ka case bhi handle karna hai: jab reconciler kisi component ko REMOVE kare, to uske saare hooks pe ghoom kar har cleanup chala do — aur uske andar ke saare components ke bhi (recursion).
gotchas: Cleanup ko async mat banao. useEffect(async () => {...}) galat hai — async function ek Promise return karta hai, cleanup function nahi. Andar ek async function banao aur usko call karo.
Unmount pe cleanup chalana bhool jaana sabse chhupa hua bug hai. Timers chalte rehte hain aur "setState on unmounted component" warnings aati hain. Ye poora app dheere-dheere dheema kar deta hai.
Cleanup mein us waqt ki closure wali values milti hain, taaza values nahi. Ye sahi hai — tumhe wahi resource band karna hai jo tumne kholaa tha.

units.title: Stage B ki deewar — Ek hi thread, aur 16ms

lessons.name: Ek thread, aur uska 16ms ka budget
lessons.desc: Browser ke paas ek frame ke liye 16.7ms hote hain. Tumhara JS unhi mein se khata hai.
lessons.what:
60fps ka matlab hai ek second mein 60 frames — matlab ek frame ke liye 1000/60 = 16.7ms.

Us 16.7ms mein browser ko ye sab karna hota hai: tumhara JS chalana, style recalculate, layout, paint, composite. Agar tumhara JS akela 100ms le le, to 6 frames chhoot gaye. User ko wo jerk ya freeze dikhta hai.

Definition: A "long task" is any single JavaScript task that occupies the main thread for more than 50ms. During a long task the page cannot respond to input at all.
lessons.why:
Aur sabse buri baat: is dauraan click bhi queue mein baith jaata hai. User ne button dabaya, kuch nahi hua, usne phir dabaya. Jab JS khatam hua to dono clicks ek saath chalenge. Ye "app hang ho gaya" wali feeling hai.

Ye sirf performance ka issue nahi hai — ye user ka bharosa hai. Ek app jo 100ms mein react karta hai wo "tez" lagta hai; jo 300ms leta hai wo "toota hua".

Kaise karna hai:

Naapne ke do tarike:

1. DevTools > Performance — recording lo, aur laal triangle wale "Long Task" blocks dhundo. Har block ke upar hover karke duration dekho.
2. PerformanceObserver — code se hi long tasks pakdo. Ye production monitoring mein bhi kaam aata hai.

visual.cap: Ek frame ka budget 16.7ms. Upar wala ek hi lamba task hai — 6 frames gaye, click 100ms baad suna gaya. Neeche wala wahi kaam chhote tukdon mein — har frame paint bhi hua aur click bhi turant suna gaya.

lessons.name: Recursion ko rok kyu nahi sakte
lessons.desc: Call stack ek dher hai. Beech mein utro to sab bhool jaoge.
lessons.what:
Socho tum recursion ke beech mein rukna chahte ho — 5000 mein se 2000 nodes ho gaye, ab browser ko ek frame do.

Nahi kar sakte. Kyunki tumhara "kahan the" wala poora record call stack mein hai. Stack se utroge to wo record gaya. Aur JS mein stack ko save karke baad mein resume karne ka koi tarika nahi hai.

Analogy: tum ek gehri almari mein 10 draawer khol chuke ho aur ab andar wale dabbe mein ho. Tumhe "kaunse draawer se aaye the" ye sirf isliye pata hai kyunki tum abhi wahan khade ho. Ghar chale gaye to wapas aakar theek wahi jagah dhundhni padegi.
lessons.why:
Isliye Fiber ne recursion chhodi. Ye sabse badi architectural insight hai poore project ki: agar tumhe kaam ko pause karna hai, to "kahan ho" wala record apne paas rakho, call stack pe mat chhodo.

Kaise karna hai:

Solution: tree ko aise banao ki har node se agla node nikal sakta ho — bina stack ke. Matlab har node ko batana padega: mera pehla bachcha kaun, mera agla bhai kaun, aur mera baap kaun.

Ye teen pointers — child, sibling, return — mil kar ek tree ko ek chalne layak list bana dete hain. Aur wahi Fiber hai.

Ab "kahan ho" sirf ek variable hai: nextUnitOfWork. Usko rakho, ruk jao, baad mein wahin se shuru kar do. Bas.
gotchas: Generators (function*) se bhi pause ho sakta hai, aur React ne shuru mein ye try bhi kiya tha. Chhoda kyunki generator sirf apni jagah se resume ho sakta hai — beech se priority badalna ya kaam phenkna mumkin nahi. Ye jaanna interview mein achha lagta hai.
Web Workers se main thread bacha sakte the — par DOM worker se chhua nahi ja sakta. Isliye wo raasta band hai.

lessons.name: Solution ka aakaar — units of work
lessons.desc: Kaam ko chhote tukdon mein todo, har tukde ke baad pucho "aur waqt hai?"
lessons.what:
Naya model ye hoga:

1. Poora kaam chhote "units" mein tootega — ek unit = ek node ka kaam.
2. Ek loop chalega jo ek unit karta hai, phir puchta hai "browser ko kuch karna hai kya?"
3. Agar haan, to loop ruk jaata hai. Browser paint karta hai, click sunta hai.
4. Browser free hote hi loop wahin se dobara shuru.

Isko cooperative scheduling kehte hain — kaam khud beech-beech mein control chhodta hai.
lessons.why:
Total time badh jaayega — yield karne ka apna kharcha hai. Par app zinda mehsoos hoga. Ye ek gehra trade-off hai: throughput vs responsiveness.

Aur ye baat React ki poori "concurrent" kahani ka aadhaar hai. Ye ek design philosophy hai: user ko ek 100ms ka freeze bura lagta hai, par 120ms ka smooth kaam accha lagta hai — chahe wo actually zyada waqt le.

Kaise karna hai:

"Browser ko kuch karna hai kya?" ka jawab dene wale do API hain:

requestIdleCallback(cb) — browser tumhe tab bulata hai jab wo free ho, aur deadline.timeRemaining() se batata hai ki kitna waqt bacha hai. Perfect fit — par Safari mein support nahi hai aur timing predictable nahi hai.

MessageChannel — ek "turant agla task" schedule karne ka tarika, setTimeout(0) se tez (jo minimum 4ms clamp hota hai). React yahi use karta hai aur khud apna 5ms ka budget rakhta hai.

Hum requestIdleCallback se shuru karenge (samajhna aasan), aur stretch goal mein MessageChannel wala scheduler banayenge.
gotchas: requestIdleCallback Safari mein nahi hai. Ek chhota polyfill (setTimeout based) rakhna padega, ya MessageChannel wala scheduler likhna padega.
Har unit ke baad timeRemaining() call karna bhi thoda mehnga hai. React har unit pe nahi, kuch units ke baad check karta hai.
Agar ek single unit khud 16ms le le (bahut bhaari component), to yielding se koi fayda nahi. Isliye units ko chhota rakhna zaroori hai — ek node, ek unit.

units.title: Fiber — Tree ko chalne layak banao

lessons.name: Fiber node — shape aur teen pointers
lessons.desc: Element ke saath kaam ki extra information. Aur ek naya rishta.
lessons.what:
Ek fiber node mein ye rehta hai:

type, props — element se aaya
dom — is fiber ka asli DOM node (agar host fiber hai)
child — pehla bachcha (saare nahi, sirf pehla)
sibling — agla bhai
return — baap (isko parent nahi, "return" kehte hain kyunki kaam khatam hone pe hum wapas yahin "return" karte hain)
alternate — purane render ka wahi fiber (Phase 12)
effectTag — kya karna hai: PLACEMENT / UPDATE / DELETION
lessons.why:
Ek node ke saare bachche ek array mein rakhne ki jagah sirf pehla bachcha rakhna, aur baaki ko bhai ki chain banana — ye trick hai. Isse har node se agla node ek fixed rule se nikal aata hai, bina kisi array index ya stack ke.

Aur wahi hume "pause karne layak" banata hai: hamari poori position ek hi pointer mein simat jaati hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Definition: A fiber is a plain object representing one unit of work, holding both the element's data and the links needed to traverse the tree without recursion.

Yaad rakho: fiber tree wahi element tree hai, bas alag tareeke se joda hua. Data same hai — sirf rishton ka roop badla hai. Ye baat samajh gaye to Fiber ka darr khatam.

visual.cap: Same tree, do roop. Left: parent → children array. Right: parent → pehla child, aur children aapas mein sibling chain. Numbers traversal ka order dikhate hain — aur wo order bilkul wahi hai jo recursion deta.

lessons.name: performUnitOfWork — ek node ka kaam
lessons.desc: DOM banao (agar nahi hai), bachon ke fibers banao, agla node return karo.
lessons.what:
Ek "unit of work" mein teen kaam hain:

1. Agar fiber ka DOM node nahi hai to bana do (abhi append mat karo!).
2. Iske bachon ke liye fibers banao aur chain mein jodo.
3. Agla fiber kaun sa hai wo return kar do — child, ya sibling, ya upar chadh ke.
lessons.why:
Har unit chhota aur bounded hai — ek node ka kaam, chahe tree kitna bhi bada ho. Isliye loop kabhi bhi ek unit ke baad ruk sakta hai. Ye predictable granularity hai, aur yahi scheduler ko kaam karne deta hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek zaroori badlav: DOM banao par append mat karo. Kyunki agar hum beech mein ruk gaye aur aadha DOM append ho gaya, to user ko adhoori UI dikhegi — jo Phase 10 ka R3 tha.

To phir append kab hoga? Sab kaam khatam hone ke baad, ek saath. Wahi Phase 12 ka commit phase hai. Abhi ke liye hum banate jayenge aur ek jagah yaad rakhenge.
gotchas: DOM ko append karna bhool jaana ab bug nahi, feature hai — par commitRoot likhna bhool gaye to screen khaali rahegi aur tum ghante barbaad karoge. Pehle ek dummy commitRoot likh do.
render() ab kuch render nahi karta — wo sirf kaam schedule karta hai. Naam ab thoda galat lagta hai; React mein bhi yahi confusion hai.
requestIdleCallback(workLoop) ko loop ke andar dobara register karna zaroori hai, warna ek hi baar chalega.

lessons.name: Work loop — pause aur resume
lessons.desc: Ek variable mein poori position. Ruko, browser ko do, wapas wahin se shuru.
lessons.what:
Ab dekho ki magic kya hai: nextUnitOfWork ek variable hai jisme hamari poori position hai. Loop ruk sakta hai, function return kar sakta hai, browser jo chahe kar sakta hai — aur jab wapas aayenge, us variable se kaam wahin se chalu ho jaayega.

Isko resumable computation kehte hain. Aur ye Fiber ka poora point hai — baaki sab (priority, suspense, concurrent) isi ek property ke upar bana hai.
lessons.why:
Ek baar tumhare paas resumable work ho, to bahut kuch mumkin ho jaata hai:

• Beech mein zyada zaroori kaam aa jaaye to usko pehle karo (priority)
• Kaam phenk do agar wo purana ho gaya (user ne aur type kar diya)
• Ek kaam ko rok ke rakho jab tak data na aaye (Suspense)

Hum in mein se koi nahi banayenge — par ab tum bata sakte ho ki ye kaise mumkin hain. Aur interview mein wahi puchha jaata hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek chhota par zaroori detail: hum wipRoot (work in progress root) rakhte hain, aur currentRoot (jo abhi screen pe hai). Kaam wipRoot pe hota hai, screen currentRoot dikhati hai.

Ye do alag trees hona hi Phase 12 ki neev hai. Aur ye ek jaana-pehchana pattern hai — graphics mein isko double buffering kehte hain: ek buffer pe likho, dusra dikhao, phir swap kar do.
gotchas: Agar pause 0 aaye to matlab tumhara tree itna chhota hai ki ek idle period mein khatam ho gaya. 10000+ nodes lo, aur CPU throttling lagao.
requestIdleCallback ka deadline browser ke mood pe depend karta hai. Kabhi 50ms milega, kabhi 1ms. Ye normal hai — code dono handle kare.
console.log ko har unit pe mat lagao — wo khud itna slow hai ki measurement bekaar ho jaayega.

lessons.name: alternate — do trees, aur swap
lessons.desc: Har fiber ke paas uska purana version hai. Kaam naye pe, dikhta purana.
lessons.what:
Har fiber ke paas ek alternate pointer hai jo pichle render ke us hi fiber ko point karta hai.

Do trees hote hain: current tree (jo abhi screen pe hai) aur work-in-progress tree (jo ban raha hai). Commit ke waqt bas currentRoot = wipRoot — aur do trees ke role swap ho jaate hain.

Definition: Double buffering means keeping two versions of a structure — one being displayed, one being written — and swapping them atomically when the new one is complete.
lessons.why:
Teen faayde, teeno bade:

1. Comparison free hai — purana fiber ek pointer door hai, dhundhna nahi padta.
2. Cancel karna free hai — wipRoot phenk do, screen ko pata bhi nahi chalega.
3. Memory reuse — React alternate fibers ko reuse karta hai instead of naye banane ke, kyunki har render pe hazaron object banana mehnga hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Jab hum ek fiber ke bachon ke fibers banate hain, to hum saath-saath uske purane bachon se compare bhi karte hain (wipFiber.alternate.child se chal kar). Yahi Stage B ka reconcile hai — bas ab wo fiber tree pe ho raha hai.

Aur compare ka nateeja ek effectTag banta hai: PLACEMENT (naya hai), UPDATE (props badle), ya DELETION (ab nahi chahiye).

lessons.name: commitRoot — sab kuch ek saath
lessons.desc: Ek recursive walk, teen effectTags, aur DOM ek hi baar mein badal jaata hai.
lessons.what:
Commit phase seedha hai: fiber tree pe ghoomo aur har fiber ka effectTag dekh ke kaam karo.

PLACEMENT → parentDom.appendChild(fiber.dom)
UPDATE → updateDom(fiber.dom, alternate.props, fiber.props)
DELETION → cleanup chalao, phir parentDom.removeChild
lessons.why:
Aur ye recursion se hi karo — aur ye jaan-boojh ke hai. Commit ko rukna nahi chahiye. Agar commit beech mein ruk jaaye to user ko adhoori UI dikhegi, jo poore design ka ulta hai.

Ye ek zaroori insight hai: Fiber ne recursion ko poori tarah nahi hataya — sirf wahan hataya jahan pause karna zaroori tha. Commit chhota aur tez hota hai (kyunki usme sirf changes hain, poora tree nahi), isliye wahan recursion bilkul theek hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek chhota par asli detail: parent DOM dhundhna. Function components ka apna DOM nahi hota, isliye fiber.return.dom null ho sakta hai. Upar chadhte jao jab tak DOM wala fiber na mile.

Wahi baat deletion mein bhi — agar delete hone wale fiber ka apna DOM nahi hai (component hai) to uske bachon mein neeche jao jab tak DOM na mile.
gotchas: DELETION case mein return karna zaroori hai — warna tum delete kiye hue subtree mein ghoomte rahoge.
domParentFiber wali loop bhool jaoge to function components ke bachche galat jagah append honge (ya crash).

PLACEMENT hamesha appendChild karta hai, isliye beech mein insert karne pe order galat ho sakta hai. Keys wale reordering ke liye insertBefore chahiye — ye ek known limitation hai, decisions.md mein likho.

lessons.name: Render phase pure kyu hona chahiye
lessons.desc: Ye phase ruk sakta hai, cancel ho sakta hai, do baar chal sakta hai. Isliye niyam sakht hain.
lessons.what:
Ab tum khud dekh sakte ho ki React itna zid kyu karta hai:

• "Render ke dauraan side effects mat karo"
• "Props aur state ko mutate mat karo"
• "StrictMode mein components do baar render hote hain"

Kyunki render phase mein tumhara component function kai baar chal sakta hai, aur uska kaam phenka ja sakta hai. Agar usne fetch kar diya ya koi global badal diya, to wo do baar hoga ya adhoora hoga.
lessons.why:
Ye poori library ka sabse gehra sabak hai: ek performance feature (interruptibility) ne API pe ek constraint (purity) daal diya.

Aur ye ek general truth hai — architecture ke faisle hamesha upar tak dikhte hain. Tum ek layer mein kuch chunte ho, aur uski keemat user-facing API mein dikhti hai. Isko chhupaya nahi ja sakta, sirf achhe se explain kiya ja sakta hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Apni library mein ek chhota StrictMode banao: dev mode mein har component function do baar call karo aur dono results compare karo. Alag aayein to warning do.

Ye 10 line ka hai aur ye tumhare project ka sabse "senior" feature hai — kyunki ye batata hai ki tum sirf feature nahi, us feature ki keemat bhi samajhte ho.
gotchas: Do baar render karne se performance dev mein aadhi ho jaayegi. Ye theek hai — production mein flag off rakho.
JSON.stringify se compare karoge to functions (event handlers) match nahi karenge. Un ko sanitize (hata) karna padega.
StrictMode effects ko bhi do baar chalata hai (React 18) — cleanup ki galtiyan pakadne ke liye. Ye stretch goal hai.

units.title: Hooks on Fiber — Aur baaki ke hooks

lessons.name: Hooks ko fiber pe le jao
lessons.desc: wipFiber.hooks, aur alternate se purane hooks. Bilkul wahi pattern.
lessons.what:
Ab hooks fiber pe rahenge: fiber.hooks = []. Aur purane hooks kahan se aayenge? fiber.alternate.hooks se.

Dekho — ye bilkul wahi pattern hai jo humne teen baar dekha hai:

Phase 6: newEl.dom = oldEl.dom
Phase 8: newEl.instance = oldEl.instance
Phase 13: fiber.hooks ← fiber.alternate.hooks
lessons.why:
Ek hi idea, teen roop: "purani cheez naye node ko pass karo." Jab tumhe ek pattern teen jagah dikhe, to wo pattern nahi — wo architecture hai. Ye baat interview mein bolne layak hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek naya kaam bhi aaya: function component ka fiber ab updateFunctionComponent se handle hoga, jisme hooks context set karke component call hota hai.

Aur setState ab seedha update nahi karega. Wo ek naya wipRoot banayega aur nextUnitOfWork set kar dega. Work loop apne aap use utha lega. Ye Stage B se ek level upar hai — ab state update aur rendering poori tarah alag ho gaye hain.
gotchas: Queue wala design pehli baar ajeeb lagta hai, par ye zaroori hai: setState turant state nahi badalta, wo ek action queue mein daalta hai jo agle render mein lagta hai. Isi se functional updates aur batching dono muft mein mil jaate hain.
wipFiber.hooks ko har render pe naya array banao, purana reuse mat karo — warna purane aur naye hooks mix ho jayenge.
setState ke andar wipRoot banate waqt currentRoot.props use karo, kisi component ka nahi — hum poore tree ko dobara render kar rahe hain.

lessons.name: useRef, useMemo, useCallback — sab ek hi cheez
lessons.desc: Ek slot jo render ke beech bacha rehta hai. Bas ussi ke alag-alag roop.
lessons.what:
Ab dekho ki baaki hooks kitne chhote hain:

useRef = ek slot jisme ek object hai {current: x}, jo kabhi nahi badalta.
useMemo = ek slot jisme value + deps hai. Deps same to purani value do, warna dobara calculate karo.
useCallback = useMemo(() => fn, deps). Bas.
useReducer = useState jisme action ko state mein badalne ka tarika tum dete ho.
lessons.why:
Jab tum ye 4 hooks khud likhoge, to hooks ka poora API ek chhoti consistent cheez lagne lagega. Aur ye ek asli library design sabak hai: ek primitive banao, baaki sab uske upar.

React ke andar bhi bas do primitives hain — useState (jo asal mein useReducer hai) aur useEffect. Baaki sab in dono ke combinations hain.

Kaise karna hai:

Har hook ka shape ek jaisa rakho: { ...data, deps }. Aur ek chhota helper getHook() likho jo purana hook nikaale aur naya slot banaye. Isse har hook 5-6 line ka reh jaata hai.

lessons.name: Effects fiber pe — aur commit ke baad
lessons.desc: Effect list fiber pe, aur commit phase ke baad ek saath flush.
lessons.what:
Effects ka logic Stage B jaisa hi hai, bas do cheezein badalti hain:

1. Effect hook fiber pe rehta hai, aur purana alternate se aata hai.
2. Effects commit phase ke baad chalte hain, kyunki tabhi DOM taiyar hota hai.

Aur ek nayi cheez: cleanup ka waqt. Purana cleanup commit ke dauraan chalna chahiye (DOM hatane se pehle), aur naya effect commit ke baad.
lessons.why:
Ab tum useEffect aur useLayoutEffect ka farak khud bana sakte ho:

useLayoutEffect — commit ke turant baad, synchronously, browser ke paint se pehle. Isse tum DOM naap kar usi frame mein badal sakte ho, bina flicker ke.
useEffect — commit ke baad, par async (paint ke baad). Isse paint block nahi hota.

Ye do line ka farak hai code mein, par user ke liye bahut bada farak hai. Aur ab tum wo farak bana ke samjhaoge, ratt ke nahi.

Kaise karna hai:

Commit ke aakhir mein do queues chalao: pehle layout effects (sync), phir queueMicrotask ya requestIdleCallback se passive effects.
gotchas: useLayoutEffect mein bhaari kaam mat karo — wo paint ko block karta hai, jo bilkul wahi problem hai jo hum Phase 10 mein theek kar rahe the.
Cleanup ko commit ke dauraan chalao, effect ko commit ke baad. Ulta karoge to purana resource naye ke saath thodi der chalega.
ref prop ko handle karna mat bhoolo — createDom mein dom bante hi ref.current = dom karna padega, warna useRef DOM ke liye kaam nahi karega.

units.title: Events & Review — Context, delegation aur architecture ka hisaab

lessons.name: Event delegation aur synthetic events
lessons.desc: Har node pe listener vs ek listener root pe. Aur React ne kya chuna aur kyu.
lessons.what:
Ab tak hum har DOM node pe seedha addEventListener lagate hain. Ye kaam karta hai, par teen problems hain:

1. 1000 buttons = 1000 listeners = memory.
2. Har update pe purana hatao naya lagao — kaam.
3. Purane browsers mein event behaviour alag-alag tha.

Event delegation ka matlab: root pe ek hi listener lagao. Event bubble hokar wahan aayega, aur event.target se pata chal jaayega ki asli mein kaunsa element tha.
lessons.why:
React 17 se pehle React saare listeners document pe lagata tha; ab wo root container pe lagata hai. Ye badla kyunki ek page pe do React apps ho sakte hain, aur document-level delegation dono ko takra deta tha.

Ye ek achha sabak hai: architecture ke faisle badalte hain jab context badalta hai. Jo React 16 mein sahi tha wo React 17 mein galat ho gaya — kyunki duniya badli, code nahi.

Kaise karna hai:

Synthetic event ek wrapper object hai jo browser ke native event ke upar banta hai, taaki har browser mein behaviour same ho.

Hum ek simple version banayenge: root pe listeners, ek map domNode → handlers, aur bubbling khud simulate karenge (target se upar chadh kar har parent ka handler chalao).

Aur decisions.md mein imaandari se likhna: ye trade-off hamare project ke liye zaroori nahi tha — humne banaya seekhne ke liye. Real trade-off tab aata hai jab thousands of nodes hon.

lessons.name: Context — data ko neeche bhejna
lessons.desc: Provider value fiber pe rakho, consumer return chain upar chadh kar dhundhe.
lessons.what:
Problem: theme ya user ko 5 level neeche bhejne ke liye har level pe prop pass karna padta hai — prop drilling.

Context ka jawab: ek Provider tree mein ek value "rakh" deta hai, aur uske neeche koi bhi component wo value seedha le sakta hai.
lessons.why:
Implementation mein ek khoobsurti hai: humare paas pehle se return pointer hai jo har fiber ko apne parent se jodta hai. To consumer ko bas upar chadhte jaana hai jab tak matching provider na mile.

Ye is baat ka achha udaharan hai ki ek accha data structure baad ke features ko kitna aasan bana deta hai. Fiber humne scheduling ke liye banaya tha — par context bhi usi se muft mein ban gaya.

Kaise karna hai:

createContext(defaultValue) ek object return karta hai jisme ek Provider component hai.

useContext(ctx) mein: wipFiber se shuru karke return chain upar chadho; jis fiber ka type === ctx.Provider ho, uske props.value lauta do. Nahi mila to default.

Aur ek imaandar baat likhna: hamara context poore tree ko re-render karega jab value badlegi, kyunki hamara setState poora root re-render karta hai. React bhi asal mein sirf consumers ko re-render karta hai par uske liye ek subscription mechanism chahiye. Ye "known limitation" likhna zaroori hai.
gotchas: Provider ki value ek object ho to har render pe naya banega, aur consumers har baar re-render honge. useMemo se stable rakho — bilkul wahi deps wali problem.
Context ko "global state" ki tarah mat use karo. Wo dependency injection ke liye hai (theme, locale, auth), high-frequency data ke liye nahi.
Hamara implementation return chain har render pe chadhta hai — O(depth). React ek stack maintain karta hai jo O(1) hai. Ye limitation likh do.

lessons.name: Architecture review — aur kya scale karega
lessons.desc: Peeche mud kar dekho. Layers ginno, limits likho, aur agla kadam batao.
lessons.what:
Ab tumne ek library bana li. Aakhri kaam hai usko samajhna — apne hi kaam ko bahar se dekhna.

Char sawaal ka jawab likho:

1. Kaunsi layer kya jaanti hai, aur kya nahi jaanti?
2. Kaunsa hissa alag renderer ke saath chal jaayega, aur kaunsa nahi?
3. Kahan-kahan O(n) hai aur kahan O(n²) ka khatra hai?
4. Agle 3 features kya honge aur kis layer mein jayenge?
lessons.why:
Ye sirf documentation nahi hai. Ye wo kaam hai jo senior engineer aur junior engineer ka farak hai. Junior batata hai ki usne kya banaya. Senior batata hai ki usne kya chuna, kya chhoda, aur kis waqt wo faisla galat ho jaayega.

Aur practically: ye document tumhare project ka sabse zyada padha jaane wala hissa hoga.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek scalability checklist chalao. Har item ke saath ek naapa hua number ya ek imaandar "pata nahi":

• 100 / 1000 / 10000 nodes pe mount aur update time
• Deeply nested tree (500 level) — crash hota hai?
• 10000-item list ko reverse karna — kitne DOM moves?
• Memory: 10000 fibers kitni RAM lete hain?
• Bundle size (minified + gzip)
• Kitne public API functions hain? (kam = behtar)
